newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via three-day system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via three-day system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York is expected to add temporary reserves to the banking system on Monday through three-day system repurchase agreements, Fed watchers said.
"We're looking for a three-day system RP coming in this morning," said Dana Saporta, economist at Stone and McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
"But with (federal) funds so tight we do have to acknowledge the possibility of an even more aggressive overnight system RP," she added.
At 1020 EST/1520 GMT, federal funds were quoted 5-3/4 percent, well above the central bank's 5-1/4 percent target for the overnight rate.
Saporta estimated the Fed's daily add need at $4.7 bilion in the remaining three days of the current two-week reserve maintenance period.
Analysts at consulting firm MMS International also expect the Fed to inject reserves into the system via three-day system repurchase agreements.
Pundits also said the Fed is expected to add permanent reserves to the banking system through a coupon pass.

"We're still looking for a coupon pass any day now ... The probability of a coupon pass tomorrow is a little greater than today because of the bill auction this afternoon. But still I wouldn't rule out anything," Saporta said.
The Treasury will sell $28.0 billion in three- and six-month bills on Monday. The bidding deadline for the auction is 1300 EST/1800 GMT.
